candidates.attacker_control: The attacker controls the HTTP Content-Type header. Dispatcher.wrapRequest() only requires the header value to contain the literal 'multipart/form-data', which can be embedded inside a malformed/expression-bearing header, so the header value is passed to commons-fileupload and, on a parse failure, is included verbatim in the exception message that becomes the OGNL-evaluated default message. In the jakarta-stream adapter, the file name taken from the multipart Content-Disposition is concatenated into the FileSizeLimitExceededException message that is likewise evaluated.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: 1) Bundle lookup could return a fixed message instead of the attacker text: verified in core/src/main/resources/org/apache/struts2/struts-messages*.properties that upload.error keys exist only for SizeLimitExceededException and IOException; InvalidContentTypeException and other parse exceptions have no key, so the code falls through to getDefaultMessage with the attacker-influenced default message. 2) The size-limit branch passes only numeric args and the bundle message is found, so that specific branch is not attacker-text-driven. 3) MessageFormat is applied after translateVariables (line 729), so it does not neutralize ${}/%{}. 4) Dispatcher requires the Content-Type to contain 'multipart/form-data', but the malicious header can include that substring, so the check does not prevent the attack. 5) The OGNL sandbox (SecurityMemberAccess; struts.excludedPackageNames=java.lang,ognl,javax in struts-default.xml) may restrict class/member access, so the sandbox-bypass-to-RCE step is not proven here, but the injection itself (untrusted text evaluated by the value stack) is directly visible in source. 6) The equivalent fix is absent: getDefaultMessage still calls translateVariables on the default message, and the multipart adapters still pass e.getMessage() as default message.
candidates.impact: Remote, unauthenticated expression/OGNL injection in the server's request-processing context. This exact code path is the documented RCE fixed as S2-045 (CVE-2017-5638): the evaluated expression executes with the application server's privileges, historically allowing arbitrary command execution and full host compromise. Even where the OGNL sandbox restricts static/member access, evaluating remote text as an expression is a critical injection primitive. A server-side fix should stop evaluating error-derived text (e.g. do not pass exception messages through translateVariables / do not use exception text as a localizable default message) in all multipart adapters.
candidates.prerequisites: Default configuration only: core servlet filter (StrutsPrepareAndExecuteFilter/PrepareOperations) creates the ActionContext and value stack before wrapping the request; struts.multipart.parser=jakarta in default.properties; JakartaMultiPartRequest/StreamMultiPartRequest registered in struts-default.xml; an unauthenticated request whose Content-Type contains 'multipart/form-data' and which fails parsing (or, for jakarta-stream, exceeds size with a crafted filename). No login, valid multipart body, or non-default setting needed.
candidates.root_cause: JakartaMultiPartRequest (and the jakarta-stream adapter) build upload error messages by passing the thrown exception's message as the defaultMessage argument of LocalizedTextUtil.findText(). LocalizedTextUtil.getDefaultMessage() then applies TextParseUtil.translateVariables() to that default message, and TextParseUtil/OgnlTextParser evaluate anything of the form ${...} or %{...} with ValueStack.findValue(). The exception message for commons-fileupload parse failures contains the attacker-supplied Content-Type header (invalid content type / no boundary), and the jakarta-stream adapter additionally builds a FileSizeLimitExceededException message from the attacker-supplied multipart filename, so untrusted text is compiled and evaluated as OGNL.
candidates.title: Unauthenticated OGNL injection via multipart parse error message (S2-045/CVE-2017-5638 class)
candidates.trace: StrutsPrepareAndExecuteFilter.doFilter (lines 91-94) -> PrepareOperations.createActionContext (value stack exists, lines 71-91) -> PrepareOperations.wrapRequest -> Dispatcher.wrapRequest (lines 791-795: Content-Type contains 'multipart/form-data' -> new MultiPartRequestWrapper) -> MultiPartRequestWrapper constructor calls multi.parse(request, saveDir) (line 85) -> JakartaMultiPartRequest.parse catch blocks call buildErrorMessage(e, ...) (lines 100-106) -> buildErrorMessage passes e.getMessage() as defaultMessage to LocalizedTextUtil.findText (lines 115-118) -> LocalizedTextUtil.findText fails all bundle lookups and calls getDefaultMessage (lines 570-580) -> getDefaultMessage applies TextParseUtil.translateVariables(message, valueStack) to the attacker-influenced default message (line 729) -> TextParseUtil.translateVariables builds an evaluator that calls stack.findValue(parsedValue) (lines 154-168) -> OgnlTextParser.evaluate extracts the ${...}/%{...} body and calls the evaluator (lines 10-81), i.e. attacker text is evaluated as an OGNL expression.
candidates.unverified: No code was executed and no exploit payload was used. The precise exception-message contents of the bundled commons-fileupload 1.3.1 were not read in this snapshot (external library), so the exact attacker string that reaches getDefaultMessage is inferred from that library's known behavior and the Struts call sites; the OGNL sandbox bypass and actual command execution were not confirmed at runtime. Only source-level evidence is claimed.

coverage_summary: Assignable snapshot: 2648 source files (Struts 2.5-SNAPSHOT). Inspected in depth: core dispatcher/filter chain (StrutsPrepareAndExecuteFilter, PrepareOperations, Dispatcher, StrutsRequestWrapper), all multipart adapters (JakartaMultiPartRequest, JakartaStreamMultiPartRequest, MultiPartRequestWrapper, MultiPartRequest, PellMultiPartRequest), localization/expression utilities (LocalizedTextUtil, TextParseUtil, OgnlTextParser, TokenHelper), OGNL plumbing (OgnlUtil, OgnlValueStack, SecurityMemberAccess), interceptors (ParametersInterceptor, FileUploadInterceptor, StaticParametersInterceptor, AliasInterceptor, CookieInterceptor read direction, TokenInterceptor surface), action mappers (DefaultActionMapper, Restful2ActionMapper), default configuration (default.properties, struts-default.xml, struts-messages*.properties), and the REST plugin content-handler/XStream path. The bulk of plugins, apps, tests, resources, and documentation (most of the 2648 files) was not exhaustively read; findings are limited to the traced paths above.
limitations: No build, execution, test, or scanner was run; the finding is source-level only and was not runtime-confirmed.

commons-fileupload 1.3.1 source is not part of the snapshot, so the exact exception message text containing the Content-Type header is inferred from that library version's documented behavior rather than verified locally.

The OGNL sandbox (SecurityMemberAccess with struts.excludedPackageNames=java.lang,ognl,javax) could constrain expression capabilities; the sandbox-bypass-to-RCE step was not verified, only the untrusted-text-to-OGNL-evaluation chain.
Historical CVE/S2 numbering is used as context for impact, not verified against advisories in this run.
Coverage is not exhaustive over 2648 files; plugin and application code outside the reviewed paths may contain additional issues that were not evaluated.

rejected_leads.lead: REST plugin XML deserialization: plugins/rest/src/main/java/org/apache/struts2/rest/handler/XStreamHandler.java lines 43-50 use a plain new XStream() and fromXML(Reader, Object), invoked from ContentTypeInterceptor (lines 60-65) for request bodies whose Content-Type selects the xml handler.
rejected_leads.reason: Real deserialization risk (S2-052/CVE-2017-9805 class) but requires the optional REST plugin and application/xml content-type handling; the core multipart OGNL path is enabled by default, unauthenticated, and has stronger, more direct source evidence, so this was not submitted as the single candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: Namespace injection / S2-057 class: DefaultActionMapper.parseNameAndNamespace takes the namespace from the request URI when struts.mapper.alwaysSelectFullNamespace=true (core/src/main/java/org/apache/struts2/dispatcher/mapper/DefaultActionMapper.java lines 336-339), and the Convention plugin sets that constant to true (plugins/convention/src/main/resources/struts-plugin.xml line 63).
rejected_leads.reason: Exploitation depends on additional application result configuration (e.g. results that interpolate namespace) and on the convention setting; the source alone does not establish attacker-controlled OGNL evaluation in this snapshot, so it remains an unconfirmed lead.

rejected_leads.lead: Dynamic method invocation / Restful2ActionMapper method selection (core/src/main/java/org/apache/struts2/dispatcher/mapper/Restful2ActionMapper.java).
rejected_leads.reason: No missing authorization check was identified in this snapshot; struts.enable.DynamicMethodInvocation defaults to false in core/src/main/resources/org/apache/struts2/default.properties, so no clear default-config vulnerability could be substantiated.

rejected_leads.lead: Other translateVariables/findValue sinks (ActionChainResult, HttpHeaderResult, StrutsResultSupport, StrutsBodyTagSupport, validation messages).
rejected_leads.reason: These evaluate values configured by the application developer rather than directly attacker-controlled request data in the default configuration; reviewed but not selected.

rejected_leads.lead: Jakarta stream multipart addFileSkippedError / buildMessage paths.
rejected_leads.reason: These are the same root cause as the submitted candidate (untrusted exception/filename text evaluated as OGNL), not a distinct issue; they are included in the candidate's trace and locations.

summary: This is the Apache Struts 2 framework at version 2.5-SNAPSHOT (mid-2016-era dependency set: commons-fileupload 1.3.1, ognl 3.1.2, xstream 1.4.8, log4j2 2.5). I traced the request path from the Struts filter through multipart parsing into the localization utility and OGNL evaluator. The single strongest source-evidenced issue is an unauthenticated OGNL/expression injection in the multipart error-handling path (the code path fixed later as S2-045 / CVE-2017-5638): a parse failure's exception message, which embeds attacker-controlled Content-Type (and, for the streaming parser, uploaded filename) text, is passed as the default message to LocalizedTextUtil.findText(), which evaluates ${...}/%{...} through TextParseUtil.translateVariables() -> OgnlTextParser -> ValueStack.findValue(). The default multipart parser (jakarta) and default filter configuration reach this code for any request whose Content-Type contains "multipart/form-data", before action mapping, so no authentication or valid upload is required. Other plausible leads (REST-plugin XStream deserialization, namespace handling) were checked and left as rejected/unconfirmed leads rather than additional candidates.
